headline: Medium risk: shared orchestration can create prompt, data, and workflow-cascade issues; no direct evidence of a hard isolation boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can consume artifacts and Prefect can orchestrate workflow metadata, so a pairwise bridge via shared files or workflow outputs is plausible. Neither profile shows a protected provenance boundary, and both are docs-only/unverified, so uncertainty pushes this above low. No direct evidence of a shared channel is present.
conditions: IF either agent ingests the other's file or workflow output as trusted instructions
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every handoff artifact
Strip executable directives from inter-agent payloads
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Require human review before replaying outputs
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on all exchanged messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch workflow-related artifacts/metadata and have network egress, so a shared workspace or API-mediated handoff could expose sensitive operational data. The profiles do not show secrets handling or a hard local-only boundary, and the interaction is undocumented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or artifact store
IF workflow metadata includes sensitive parameters or secrets
mitigations: Separate storage buckets per agent
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Disable automatic artifact syncing
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on shared outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows exposes REST/GRPC APIs and Prefect calls GitHub APIs, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared OAuth scopes. That makes direct capability conflict possible only under unusual orchestration, with limited evidence of contention.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same repository, database, or workspace
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable credentials
mitigations: Assign disjoint write targets
Use per-agent credentials
Add lock files or lease tokens
Schedule writes sequentially
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both profiles are orchestration/data-engineering systems, so one agent's outputs can plausibly become the other's inputs. Without a documented verification step, Prefect could treat Argo-produced artifacts or metadata as authoritative, creating a default cascade risk even though the exact pipeline is not evidenced.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Argo outputs without validation
IF downstream actions are triggered from workflow metadata alone
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require checksum or signature checks
Log source provenance on every handoff
Block automatic execution from untrusted outputs
requires-engineering: add policy gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source workflow tools with docs-only profiles and no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The compliance pathway is therefore not evidenced; only a generic overlap in workflow metadata/artifacts exists, so any breach would require additional deployment-specific configuration.
conditions: IF deployment policy assigns regulated data to either workflow engine
IF retention or residency settings differ across the two systems
mitigations: Document data-class handling for each agent
Align retention settings
Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata
Review residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: add compliance policy checks to orchestration
